transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-25 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Miller (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Gomez (Redwood Security), Marta Alvarez (CISO, Oceanic), Tom Reed (Head of Infra, Oceanic), Sofia Khan (Compliance, Oceanic)

Summary: quick run through incident response, desired RTO/RPO, what Redwood can offer on Dedicated / Private stacks, and operational artifacts we can provide (SOC2, audit logs, KMS options).

[00:00] Ethan: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time today. Quick intro

- i'm ethan, our AE, priya is our solutions eng and carlos handles security ops. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Marta: doing well, thanks. we wanted to walk through incident response and BCDR, clarify RTO/RPO expectations, and understand your escalation path

- regulators are asking for specifics.
[00:22] Priya: great, that's exactly what we wanted to cover. we'll start with a high-level of our incident severity matrix then dive into RTO/RPO for our hosted vs dedicated vs private options.
[00:30] Tom: quick callout

- our bar is pretty high for transactional systems, regulator expects RTO ~1 hour for critical flows and RPO around 15 minutes. if we go dedicated or private we may need faster SLAs.
[00:44] Carlos: thanks Tom, understood. to set expectations: for Redwood Hosted our standard operational playbook aims for major incident RTO of 1-2 hours and RPO is typically within 5-10 minutes for KV / cache warm-up dependent workloads; with Dedicated you can get tighter guarantees since you control capacity and we can configure synchronous replication and region pinning.
[01:05] Marta: can you quantify uptime SLA tiers? our procurement wants clear credit language.
[01:12] Ethan: yes. our public tiers are 99.9% for hosted, 99.95% for Dedicated by default; we can negotiate 99.99% for enterprise contracts with multi-region active-active. credits are pro-rated based on monthly uptime percentage

- we can share the exact formula in the SLA doc. i'll include that in the next_steps.
[01:29] Sofia: and how do you measure availability? is it per-route or overall service?
[01:35] Priya: we measure per-route availability for critical endpoints (generation, embeddings) and also provide token-level latency metrics. the SLA measurement window is UTC monthly; we exclude scheduled maintenance windows which are communicated 72 hours in advance.
[01:48] Tom: what's your maintenance blackout policy? some of our batch jobs run overnight, need to coordinate.
[01:54] Ethan: we'll coordinate. Dedicated lets you set maintenance windows and preferred blackout windows

- we'll capture that as an action item.
[02:02] Marta: incident escalation

- we need to know who gets paged, what are severity levels, and expected response times.
[02:08] Carlos: we use a standard severity matrix: Sev1 (critical outage impacting production traffic)

- pager to on-call within 5 minutes, escalation to incident manager and director within 15-30 minutes; Sev2 (degraded performance)

- acknowledgement within 30 minutes; Sev3 (non-urgent)

- tracked via ticket. For enterprise customers we can map names and phone numbers in our on-call roster and provide a dedicated Slack channel / War Room.
[02:33] Marta: and what's your escalation chain after initial triage? root cause analysis timelines?
[02:37] Carlos: initial incident postmortem (summary) within 72 hours; full RCA with mitigation steps typically within 14 days. if requested, we can accelerate RCA timelines for Business Critical incidents and provide more frequent status updates.
[02:52] Tom: can you walk through a recent incident example

- how you failed over and what the RTO was?
[02:57] Priya: sure

- last quarter we had a regional network degradation; for customers on multi-zone Dedicated we failed over to a standby region using our smart routing; observed RTO ~45 minutes for that cohort

- the hosted customers saw higher latencies but no data loss due to prefix/KV caching. there was a short period of increased tail latency. transcript note: slight word swap there, some customers had sticky sessions but we mitigated via re-routing.
[03:26] Sofia: about data residency and backup retention

- how long do you keep backups and where are they stored?
[03:32] Carlos: backups are stored in region of deployment by default. for Dedicated and Private you can specify region or on-prem. default snapshot retention is 30 days, longer retention tiers available (90/365) as an add-on. backups are encrypted at-rest with service keys; we support customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS or HSM integration for Dedicated/Private.
[03:51] Marta: we need to use our KMS keys for encryption

- can you support bring-your-own-key?
[03:56] Carlos: yes

- BYOK via KMS is supported for data-at-rest encryption on Dedicated and Private. for Hosted we offer an option to use CMKs in certain regions; we'll confirm exact cloud provider constraints in the follow-up.
[04:08] Tom: audit logging

- how granular, how long, and how do we access logs for audits?
[04:13] Priya: audit logs capture control plane actions, API calls, user sign-ins, RBAC changes, and system-level alerts. default retention 90 days with ability to export to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog/QRadar) via secure push or S3. access is RBAC-controlled; logs are immutable and time-stamped.
[04:31] Marta: do logs include payloads or PII? we have strict rules around not storing customer payloads.
[04:36] Carlos: by default we do not store full request payloads for hosted generation; we log metadata and hashes for tracing. For Dedicated/Private you can opt-in to store request bodies, but given your compliance we recommend not storing payloads, only metadata.
[04:50] Sofia: SSO and RBAC

- we need SAML + SCIM provisioning and fine-grained roles for auditors vs operators.
[04:58] Priya: supported

- SAML 2.0 SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and customizable RBAC roles (Admin, DevOps, Auditor, ReadOnly). we can map your LDAP groups to roles and provide periodic syncs.
[05:11] Tom: one point on network

- do you offer private link or VPC peering?
[05:15] Ethan: yes, Dedicated can be deployed inside customer VPC via VPC peering or privatelink depending on cloud. Private offering (on-prem) is also available for high-regulated workloads. we'll include a network diagram option in the follow-up.
[05:26] Marta: how do SLA credits get calculated when there is a partial degradation of routes vs full outage?
[05:31] Ethan: credits are proportional to impacted routes and time below the SLA threshold. e.g., if route A is affected 10% of the month below 99.95, credit formula prorates against monthly fee. i'll send the formal SLA wording.
[05:44] Tom: about RPO

- you mentioned 5-10 minutes earlier, but our bar is 15. what's realistically achievable for transactional data?
[05:51] Priya: for transactional workloads we recommend Dedicated with synchronous replication to a standby region

- that gets you sub-15 minute RPO in practice. for most workloads our KV cache approach reduces perceived data loss, but true RPO depends on replication strategy.
[06:06] Marta: any special steps for regulatory audit support? we will likely need evidence for controls, SOC2 artifacts, encryption attestations, and an audit point of contact.
[06:15] Carlos: we provide SOC 2 Type II report, encryption and key management details, and a named security contact for audits. we can provide redacted logs and artefacts under NDA

- we'll include this in next steps.
[06:26] Ethan: action item recap in a second. quick question

- do you anticipate moving directly to Dedicated or start with Hosted for a pilot?
[06:34] Tom: prefer a pilot on Dedicated if possible; procurement is pushing for a 3-6 month pilot with performance benchmarks.
[06:40] Priya: that's doable

- for a Dedicated pilot we'll propose a minimal footprint and run a joint benchmark. we can also offer a short-term commitment.
[06:49] Marta: benchmarks should include failover scenarios and DR runbooks.
[06:52] Priya: absolutely. we'll run a failover test in the tabletop exercise.
[06:57] Sofia: last piece

- escalation contact lists. Can we get a diagram that shows who Redwood will call, and expected SLAs per severity?
[07:05] Carlos: yes

- i'll prepare an escalation flow diagram showing on-call, escalation timers, and notification channels (pager, phone, slack, email).
[07:12] Ethan: ok wrapping up, i'll send SOC2, draft SLA, and a proposed week for the DR tabletop. Priya will share network diagrams and logging samples; Carlos will share escalation flow.
[07:21] Marta: thanks all, this was helpful. we'll review materials and circle back with preferred pilot dates.
[07:27] Ethan: great

- thanks everyone, talk soon.
